title: Professional Basics for Missouri CDS Caregivers: Call-Offs, Boundaries and Privacy
description: Being a great CDS caregiver is about more than the tasks. Here are the professional basics from our Attendant Orientation: showing up, calling off the right way, dignity in someone's home, keeping boundaries, and protecting their privacy.
end: Thank you for showing up for someone.

parts.head: Professional basics for CDS caregivers
parts.sub: Showing up, call-offs, dignity, boundaries, privacy
parts.text: Being a great CDS caregiver is about more than the tasks. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Here are the professional basics: showing up, calling off the right way, dignity, boundaries, and privacy.

parts.head: It's most of the job
parts.sub: Treat the schedule as a promise
parts.text: Showing up is most of the job. The person you care for planned their day around you. When you don't come, they may not eat, bathe, or get out of bed. Be on time, every shift, and treat the schedule as a promise.

parts.head: Call as early as you can
parts.sub: Agree on notice ahead of time
parts.text: Sometimes you can't come. When that happens, call them as early as you possibly can, not a few minutes before the shift. Agree ahead of time how much notice they need, and tell them early about vacations and appointments.

parts.head: Never assume someone will cover
parts.text: And never assume someone else will cover for you. That's what their backup plan is for, and they need time to use it.

parts.head: It's their home
parts.sub: Knock. Ask first. Cover them during care.
parts.text: You're in someone's home, helping with the most private parts of their life. Knock. Ask before you move their things. Cover them during personal care. And talk to them, not about them.

parts.head: Words matter
parts.sub: Demeaning words can be reported as emotional abuse
parts.text: Never talk to them in a demeaning way, even as a joke. Degrading words, or profanity aimed at them, can be reported as emotional abuse.

parts.head: Keep it professional
parts.sub: No borrowing, lending, gifts of value or personal errands
parts.text: Keep the relationship professional. Don't borrow money, and don't lend it. Don't accept gifts of value. Don't use their car for personal errands, and don't bring your own chores, family, or friends into their home. Warmth is wonderful. Blurred lines are not.

parts.head: What happens in the home stays there
parts.sub: No talking, posting or photos about them
parts.text: What happens in the home stays there. Don't discuss their health, money, or household with your friends or family. Never post about them, or photograph them or their home, on social media. And don't share their address, phone number, or papers with anyone.

parts.head: Who you can talk to
parts.text: Talk about their care only with them, their chosen representative, and us. Their health information is protected by federal law.

parts.head: Pay questions? Call us.
parts.sub: We can't discuss payroll by email
parts.text: One more privacy note. We can't discuss your payroll by email, so call us for anything about your pay.

parts.head: The basics still apply
parts.sub: They protect the relationship you already have
parts.text: If the person you care for is your own mom or grandpa, these basics still apply. They protect the relationship you already have.
Questions? Call us at 417-218-2888, Monday to Friday, nine to four. Thank you for showing up for someone. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS.
